rv.q: Sensitively discussing themes of grief, family and community, this slow-burning drama satisfyingly blends humour, heart and melancholy.
Heart Wall is poignant and thought-provoking: with a tighter focus, it could deliver even more impact.

Katie Greenall’s production also lacks sufficient drive to make the mundane-cum-tragic events sufficiently compelling. Franky (Rowan Robinson), a recent graduate who has a flat in London with her boyfriend Alfie and a job in an office near Buckingham Palace, returns home to the north of England for the weekend without notifying her parents.
Heart Wall is a beautifully structured, heartfelt piece that explores how death and life awkwardly co-exist in a way that feels fresh and true.
All in all, Heart Wall is alright, but could be better.
